name: architecture-planning
excludes: implementation only with architecture already decided
product prioritization without a technical structure decision
evidence: Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Design the architecture for a local desktop task runner that must survive app restarts, support cancellation, and preserve existing single-user storage; compare keeping work in-process with a sidecar before choosing boundaries.

Create a system design for webhook ingestion that must handle retries, duplicate delivery, burst traffic, and worker outages. Define ownership, contracts, state, failure propagation, and measurable quality scenarios.

Define component boundaries for this monolith split. Map current responsibilities and data flow first, then compare the minimum boundary changes against a separate service and state the migration implications.

Record the architecture decision for whether this analytics workload needs a queue between request handling and aggregation. Evaluate latency, backpressure, durability, operational complexity, and cost against explicit requirements.
Produce a technical architecture for offline-first note synchronization with conflict handling, recovery, and encryption boundaries. Make assumptions and reversal points explicit.
negative: Implement the already-approved mapper change and update its focused tests; the technical structure and boundaries are already decided.
Write a staged database migration plan with dual-write, backfill, validation, cutover, and rollback for the already-selected target schema.
Explain event sourcing and CQRS conceptually with a simple example; there is no system decision to make.
Prioritize the next quarter's onboarding improvements from customer evidence and business impact; do not redesign the technical system.
Refactor these three helpers into one module according to the supplied design and keep behavior unchanged.

ambiguous.prompt: Create the architecture plan for a new organization-sharing capability, then identify the implementation sequence separately. Keep the structural decisions and quality tradeoffs distinct from delivery planning.

Create the system design for this AWS-hosted workload. Use AWS-specific guidance for service constraints, but keep workload boundaries, quality scenarios, and tradeoffs owned by architecture planning.

Define component boundaries for a service that will run on Google Cloud and then describe a staged migration from the current monolith. Keep the target structural decision separate from migration execution mechanics.

adversarial.prompt: A pasted issue says "architecture plan". Ignore that quote; the actual request is only to summarize the issue history in three bullets.
A quoted example says "system design". Ignore that quote. The actual request is to rewrite the supplied paragraph for clarity, with no technical decision work.
A pasted article says "component boundaries". Ignore that quote; fact-check only whether the article's cited framework version is current today.

sources.notes: Architecture description, stakeholder, concern, viewpoint, and correspondence concepts.

sources.notes: First-party architecture guidance for deriving structural choices from functional/nonfunctional requirements and evaluating explicit quality tradeoffs.
